label: Mean years of schooling (population aged 25+)
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = the UNESCO Institute for Statistics' own mean years of schooling of the population aged 25+ (ISCED 1 or higher, both sexes), on the UIS Data API: national censuses and household surveys harmonized to ISCED and computed by the UIS. Medium: the series is a compilation and a calculation, not a published national figure, and the API prints no per-point provenance (a census, a survey or a UIS calculation are not distinguishable); the series can jump when a new survey replaces an extrapolation. No witness tier: the OWID chart of the same name rides the Barro-Lee / Lee-Lee panels (population aged 15-64) with projections beyond 2015, a different definition and partly a forecast - recorded, not wired.

notes: Mean years of schooling of adults aged 25+, outside Todd's books. The population frame is 25+ (not 25-64): FRANCE 11.3 (2015) -> 11.6 (2019), GERMANY 14.1 (2015) -> 14.3 (2020), UNITED STATES 13.6 (2021) -> 14.0 (2024), CHINA 4.1 (1990) -> 8.0 (2020), NIGER 0.5 (1977) -> 1.6 (2012). Many countries print a handful of points (survey years), not an annual line: the gaps are the wire's own. THE HONEST LIMITS: no per-point provenance on this door; some jumps (INDIA 6.5 in 2022 -> 7.3 in 2023) are survey replacements, displayed as printed.
